rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §1 writes docs/research/what-turned-a-landing-back.html and docs/figures/what-turned-a-landing-back/, and §2's negative-control log goes under the run directory; no gate writes to a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §1's root-cause framing is honest (three candidates, each with what it must explain, matching the code at promotion_scope.py:1672-1741), but §2's mechanism samples one instant immediately after the commit returns and so cannot observe the class of event its own Why names.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §1 is one investigation (a doc plus the script reproducing its single finding); §2's two mechanisms serve one goal and close on one receipt field and one test file.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — s3 correctly declares depends-on s1, and the plan-level standalone claim holds (no other plan references this plan; only docs/sprints/S26.html does), but §1's deliverable says its output "is an input to §2" while the f-alnrtc-002 followup and the absence of a §1→§2 depends-on edge declare §2 independent.
